messages.subject: Assistance needed, error in part 5
parts:
Dear all, 

I'm hoping to find some help with a problem I've encountered using GGIR. 

I'm using sleeplog as a guider for the sleep analysis in part 4. When running the code, it all seems to work fine. The outputs from part 2 and part 4 look normal and good and the output from part 4 correctly identifies the sleeplog (see picture below). 


However, in part 5, it does not pick up the sleeplog and reverts to using HDZAC as the guider (see picture below).



I've tried to identify the problem and tried multiple options with the code and tried multiple other things, including renaming the Excel files, renaming the id names, using different idloc options, but none of this seems to solve the problem. The only thing that I noticed is in the ID name, where all ID names are the same (part 2, part 4 and the sleeplog ID name is GAMES01), but in part 5 the ID name changes to GAMES01.csv

If I could get some help with potentially identifying the problem and how I can fix it, that would be most appreciated! 

Below I have attached the code and I'm happy to provide full outputs if needed! I appreciate I don't have to write out the full shell function, but wanted to see if I could identify the problem :)

Warm regards, 
Lara

Hi Lara,

I think your expectation is not correct. GGIR estimates sleep by combining sleeplog (guider) and acc-based sustained inactivity bouts (sibs): The sibs that overlap with the guider define the exact sleep onset and wakeup time. The vignette also makes an attempt to explain that. This is why sleep onset and wakeup time are unlikely to match exactly the sleeplog.

If you do not trust the accelerometer and want to fully rely on the guider (your sleeplog) then set argument relyonguider = TRUE, however I intentionally did not use that as default because often we want to rely on the accelerometer to tell us the exact timing while the sleeplog is nothing more than a way to help guide the accelerometer, hence the name guider.

Best wishes,

Vincent
